title: Hyperplane reduction of a non-equidimensional completion
statement: Let $(A,\mathfrak m)$ be a catenary Noetherian local domain, let $B=\widehat A$ be its maximal-ideal completion, and suppose a minimal prime $\mathfrak q$ of $B$ has $1<d=\dim(B/\mathfrak q)<\dim A$, where $d$ is the least dimension of a minimal-prime quotient of $B$. There exist a nonzero $f\in\mathfrak m$, a prime $\mathfrak p$ of $A$ minimal over $fA$, and a minimal prime $\mathfrak r$ of the maximal-ideal completion $\widehat{A/\mathfrak p}$ such that $\dim(A/\mathfrak p)=\dim A-1$ and $\dim(\widehat{A/\mathfrak p}/\mathfrak r)=d-1$. In particular $0<d-1<\dim(A/\mathfrak p)$. [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring] [def-weil-pbc-adic-completion] [def-weil-pbc-krull-dimension-ring] Here a domain is a nonzero commutative ring without zero divisors, local means that $\mathfrak m$ is the unique maximal ideal, and a minimal prime over an ideal is a prime containing that ideal with no strictly smaller prime containing it. Catenary means that between any comparable primes the lengths of finite strict chains have a finite bound and all saturated chains have the same length; a chain is saturated if no prime can be inserted between consecutive terms.

source.place: Tag 0AW3, lemma-not-formally-catenary, d>1 paragraph: prime avoidance hyperplane; prime-quotient refinement of the omitted formal-catenarity inference, under the catenarity hypothesis available in the contradiction argument.

proof.text: Put $N=\dim A$ and $\mathfrak n=\mathfrak mB$. The completion is Noetherian by [lem-weil-pbc-adic-completion-noetherian] and local with maximal ideal $\mathfrak n$ by [lem-weil-pbc-local-completion-local-ring]. Quotients are Noetherian since generators of an inverse-image ideal map to generators, and quotients by proper ideals of a local ring are local by prime correspondence. All their dimensions are finite by [lem-weil-pbc-noetherian-local-finite-krull-dimension]. By [lem-weil-pbc-noetherian-finitely-many-minimal-primes], list the minimal primes of $B$ other than $\mathfrak q$ as $\mathfrak q_1,\ldots,\mathfrak q_s$. For each $i$, [lem-sc-finite-minimal-primes-over-ideal] gives finitely many primes minimal over $\mathfrak q+\mathfrak q_i$. Let $\mathcal R$ consist of those primes in these lists for which $\dim(B/\mathfrak a)>0$. This is a finite set; it may be empty.

source.place: Tag 0AW3, lemma-not-formally-catenary, d>1 paragraph: the components of the intersection with the other components; algebra.tex Tags 0316, 05GI, 00KQ, 00FR

proof.text: Every $\mathfrak a\in\mathcal R$ is strictly smaller than $\mathfrak n$, since its quotient has positive dimension; the same holds for $\mathfrak q$ since $d>1$. Their contractions to $A$ are primes strictly smaller than $\mathfrak m$: otherwise they contain $\mathfrak mB=\mathfrak n$. Also $\mathfrak m\ne0$, since $N>d>1$ whereas a local domain with zero maximal ideal is a field of dimension zero. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-prime-avoidance] to the ideal $\mathfrak m$ and the finite list consisting of $(0)$, the contraction of $\mathfrak q$, and the contractions of all members of $\mathcal R$. We obtain $0\ne f\in\mathfrak m$ whose image belongs neither to $\mathfrak q$ nor to any member of $\mathcal R$. The inclusion of $(0)$ handles even the case $\mathcal R=\varnothing$.

source.place: Tag 0AW3, lemma-not-formally-catenary, choice of f by prime avoidance; Tag 00DS, lemma-silly

proof.text: The image $\bar f$ in the local domain $C=B/\mathfrak q$ is a nonzero element of its maximal ideal. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-dimension-quotient-nonzerodivisor] to obtain $\dim(C/\bar fC)=d-1$. Choose a chain attaining this finite dimension and lift its first prime to $B$. By [lem-weil-pbc-prime-contains-minimal-prime], a prime $P$ minimal over $\mathfrak q+fB$ lies below that first prime. Appending $P$ if necessary shows $\dim(B/P)\ge d-1$; the reverse inequality follows because all chains above $P$ occur in $B/(\mathfrak q+fB)$. Thus $\dim(B/P)=d-1>0$. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-noetherian-height-quotient-bound] with one equation in $C$, at the prime $P/\mathfrak q$. Its image in $C/\bar fC$ is minimal, hence has height zero. Therefore $P/\mathfrak q$ has height at most one. In particular there cannot be two strict inclusions of primes between $\mathfrak q$ and $P$.

source.place: Tag 0AW3, lemma-not-formally-catenary, component of dimension d-1; Tag 00KW, lemma-one-equation

proof.text: We show that $P$ is minimal over $fB$. Take $T\subseteq P$ minimal over $fB$, and a minimal prime $\mathfrak b$ of $B$ contained in $T$, using [lem-weil-pbc-prime-contains-minimal-prime] twice. If $\mathfrak b=\mathfrak q$, then $T$ contains $\mathfrak q+fB$, so minimality of $P$ over this ideal gives $T=P$. Otherwise $\mathfrak b=\mathfrak q_i$ for some $i$. Choose $\mathfrak a$ minimal over $\mathfrak q+\mathfrak q_i$ inside $P$ by the same cited existence result. Since $\dim(B/\mathfrak a)\ge\dim(B/P)=d-1>0$, it belongs to $\mathcal R$. The inclusion $\mathfrak q\subsetneq\mathfrak a$ is strict because distinct minimal primes are incomparable. Also $\mathfrak a\subsetneq P$ is strict since $f\notin\mathfrak a$ but $f\in P$. These two strict inclusions contradict the height bound established in Step 3. Thus only $T=P$ is possible. This supplies explicitly the component-separation argument implicit in the source.

source.place: Tag 0AW3, lemma-not-formally-catenary, d>1 paragraph: avoiding the positive-dimensional intersections

proof.text: Let $\mathfrak p=P\cap A$. Choose $\mathfrak p_0\subseteq\mathfrak p$ minimal over $fA$ by [lem-weil-pbc-prime-contains-minimal-prime]. The map $A\to B$ is flat by [lem-weil-pbc-local-completion-faithfully-flat], so [lem-sc-flat-going-down] gives a prime $T\subseteq P$ contracting to $\mathfrak p_0$. Since $f\in\mathfrak p_0$, we have $f\in T$, and Step 4 forces $T=P$. Consequently $\mathfrak p_0=\mathfrak p$, proving minimality over $fA$. Moreover $P$ is minimal over $\mathfrak pB$: any prime between $\mathfrak pB$ and $P$ contains $f$ and equals $P$. The completion isomorphism [lem-weil-pbc-local-completion-quotient] identifies $\widehat{A/\mathfrak p}$ with $B/\mathfrak pB$. Thus $\mathfrak r=P/\mathfrak pB$ is a minimal prime of that completion and its quotient is $B/P$, of dimension $d-1$.

Finally apply [lem-weil-pbc-noetherian-height-quotient-bound] in $A$ with the single equation $f$ at $\mathfrak p$. Minimality makes the corresponding prime of $A/fA$ have height zero, so $\operatorname{ht}(\mathfrak p)\le1$. Since $A$ is a domain and $0\ne f\in\mathfrak p$, the chain $(0)\subsetneq\mathfrak p$ has length one, hence is saturated. A chain of maximum length in $A/\mathfrak p$ lifts to a saturated chain from $\mathfrak p$ to $\mathfrak m$. Prepending $(0)$ gives a saturated chain from $(0)$ to $\mathfrak m$. A chain attaining $N$ also has these endpoints and is saturated. By the assumed catenarity their lengths coincide, giving $1+\dim(A/\mathfrak p)=N$. Because $1<d<N$, we have $0<d-1<N-1=\dim(A/\mathfrak p)$, as required.

Checks against each cited statement: Step 2: m is not contained in any listed contraction (each a in R is strictly below mB). Step 3: the dimension drops to d−1 in B/q because f̄ is a nonzero nonunit of a domain; Ideal.exists_minimalPrimes_le gives P minimal over q+fB with dim B/P = d−1; the height bound with t=1 gives ht(P/q) ≤ 1. Step 4: if T ⊆ P is minimal over fB and contains q_i, then a prime a minimal over q+q_i inside P is in R (this uses d>1), and q ⊊ a ⊊ P contradicts ht ≤ 1, so P is minimal over fB. Step 5: flat going-down gives T ⊆ P over p0, which forces p0 = p; local-completion-quotient with n = m/p identifies the completion of A/p with B/pB, so r = P/pB. Step 6: ht p = 1 plus catenarity of A (saturated chains (0)…m) gives dim A/p = N−1. Edge cases checked: fields and DVRs are excluded; d=2; empty R; non-reduced B; d=1 correctly falls outside. The parent lem-per-ratliff step uses exactly this clause. No duplicates (searched 0AW3, formally catenary, hyperplane).
